extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students, journalists and researchers interested in UK public policy
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the stated goals, implementation instruments and evaluative points of the UK Conservative government's 'Levelling Up' policy as described on the Wikipedia article (including the 2022 White Paper, funds, missions and criticisms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase pay, employment and productivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed as one of the 12 missions in the Levelling Up White Paper (aimed to be achieved by 2030).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as a national mission for 2030; part of the White Paper's set of measurable aims for the whole of government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic public investment in R&D outside south-east to rise by at least 40%
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit numeric mission from the White Paper: domestic public investment in R&D outside the south-east to rise by at least 40% (by 2030).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A concrete, regionally-targeted funding metric included among the 12 missions; used as a performance/target metric for regional rebalancing.

rubrics_metrics.name: London-style public transport connectivity across the UK
rubrics_metrics.description: White Paper mission aiming to deliver London-style public transport connectivity across the UK (one of the 12 missions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets improvements in local/regional public transport connectivity as an explicit dimension of levelling-up success by 2030.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationwide broadband
rubrics_metrics.description: White Paper mission to achieve nationwide broadband (one of the 12 missions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Digital connectivity is an explicit mission; the Islands Forum and other mechanisms are described to address connectivity in island areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixing the education gap
rubrics_metrics.description: Named as a mission in the White Paper: targeting and reducing educational performance gaps (aimed to be achieved by 2030).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The White Paper states areas with weak education performance will be targeted for extra investment; education outcomes are a core evaluative dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skills training
rubrics_metrics.description: White Paper mission focusing on improving skills training (one of the 12 missions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes reference elsewhere to apprenticeships and a National Skills Fund as implementation instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrowing life expectancy gap (UK-wide rise of five years by 2035)
rubrics_metrics.description: White Paper mission that includes narrowing the life expectancy gap, with an explicit metric: a UK-wide rise of five years by 2035.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mission includes a longer-term numeric health outcome (2035 horizon) as an evaluative metric for the levelling-up agenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rise in wellbeing
rubrics_metrics.description: A mission in the White Paper to increase wellbeing across the UK (one of the 12 missions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wellbeing is included as a broad outcome metric, complementary to economic and health measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decreased inequalities
rubrics_metrics.description: White Paper mission to decrease inequalities (one of the 12 missions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An explicit equity-focused mission; overlaps with other missions such as pay, life expectancy and education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rise in overall number of first-time homebuyers
rubrics_metrics.description: White Paper mission to increase the overall number of first-time homebuyers (one of the 12 missions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Housing access/homeownership is treated as a measurable outcome for the levelling-up programme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crime reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: White Paper mission to reduce crime (one of the 12 missions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crime reduction is specified as an outcome to be improved under the levelling-up agenda by 2030.

rubrics_metrics.name: Devolution in England
rubrics_metrics.description: White Paper mission to increase devolution in England (one of the 12 missions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes specific lists of areas eligible for devolution deals; the policy frames devolution as a structural means to deliver levelling-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tiered ranking of local authorities by need for Levelling Up Fund bids
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementation instrument: local authorities were ranked into three tiers by need and invited to submit project bids to the Levelling Up Fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in the 2020 Treasury spending review / initial fund rounds; selection by 'tiers' shaped eligibility and bidding processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-round funding focus areas: transport, town centre/high-street regeneration, cultural investment
rubrics_metrics.description: The first round of Levelling Up Fund bids focused on transport projects, town centre and high street regeneration, and cultural investment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of funded project types are given, with specific award totals cited for illustrative projects and places.

rubrics_metrics.name: White Paper provisions for affordable housing
rubrics_metrics.description: The White Paper includes sections making provisions for affordable housing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Housing policy and targets (e.g., first-time buyers mission) are part of the White Paper's stated interventions; critics noted the level of support for affordable housing was insufficient in some targets (e.g., new homes per year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Target extra investment to areas with weak education performance
rubrics_metrics.description: The White Paper states that areas with weak education performance will be targeted for extra investment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education attainment/attainment gaps are explicitly named as a focus for targeted interventions under levelling up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Islands Forum for island authorities to coordinate and communicate on issues (e.g., broadband)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy mechanism: establish an 'Islands Forum' enabling local authorities and island communities (Orkney, Shetland, Western Isles, Anglesey, Isle of Wight) to work together on common issues like broadband and communicate directly with government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described as a devolved/consultative mechanism aimed at addressing geography-specific connectivity and infrastructure challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decentralisation of the £2.6 billion UK Shared Prosperity Fund to local leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy instrument: a £2.6 billion UK Shared Prosperity Fund will be decentralised to local leaders as part of levelling up/devolution arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funds devolved to local decision-makers are presented as an implementation principle to deliver local priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Local Government Pension Scheme (LGPS) assets to support local investment
rubrics_metrics.description: White Paper commitment to direct more money from Local Government Pension Scheme pots to support investment in local areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a financing/investment instrument to channel private/public pension assets into regional development.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2030 (and where stated 2035) target horizons for judging missions
rubrics_metrics.description: The White Paper's 12 missions are presented as aims to be achieved by 2030 (some outcomes, e.g., life-expectancy rise, reference 2035).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The White Paper sets explicit time horizons for evaluating success; Michael Gove later described 2030 as the reference point for judging implementation progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for clear success criteria/metrics to determine impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism by the Industrial Strategy Council that the plans were 'thinly spread' and that the scheme's lack of success criteria would make it hard to determine its impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied evaluative standard: policy programmes should include clearly defined, measurable success criteria and monitoring arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation methodology should use standard indicators of poverty (avoid politically skewed classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported criticism (Financial Times) that the methodology used to determine which areas would receive funds 'ignored most standard indicators of poverty' and classified some wealthier areas as 'priority one'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied selection criterion: fund allocation methodology should rely on accepted poverty/deprivation indicators to target the most deprived areas and avoid partisan bias or skewed classifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and accountability of fund allocation (avoid 'pork barrel' politics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics accused the government of 'pork barrel politics' and highlighted analyses showing Conservative-run areas receiving higher per-capita grants in some rounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied requirement: allocation processes should be transparent, use published criteria, and be auditable to guard against political bias.
